abstract: Background: Cancer metabolic reprogramming varies across tumour types and nutrient environments, complicating the identification of robust metabolic biomarkers and therapeutic targets. We developed a constraint based pancancer framework to identify medium robust metabolic alterations and broadly effective candidate enzyme targets. Methods: Transcriptomic profiles from 33 TCGA cancer types were integrated with Recon3D to reconstruct cancer and healthy tissue specific genome scale metabolic models. Parsimonious multiobjective metabolite flow variability analysis was performed under five nutrient conditions to classify differential rates of metabolite synthesis, uptake, and secretion. An extended Anticancer Target Discovery framework incorporating fuzzy multiobjective optimization was employed to evaluate candidate enzyme perturbations based on cancer cell inhibition, ATP suppression, preservation of healthy tissue metabolism, and robustness across nutrient conditions. Findings: The models predicted recurrent increases in cardiolipin-related lipid synthesis and aromatic amino acid metabolism, enhanced uptake of essential amino acids and choline, and elevated lactate secretion across multiple cancer medium combinations. CRLS1 emerged as the most broadly effective predicted enzyme target, satisfying the treatment criteria across all 165 cancer medium combinations, whereas PGS1 and PTPMT1 exhibited broad but incomplete coverage. These findings highlight mitochondrial phospholipid metabolism as a potential shared vulnerability across cancer types and provide testable candidates for metabolomic and experimental validation.
